newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins firm on US payroll data.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins firm on US payroll data.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds firmed on U.S. payroll data on Friday, after steadying following a rise on speculation about Russia's debt rating for its Eurobond issue, dealers said.
Finance minister Alexander Livshits said on Tuesday that the rating should be known in the next 10 days.
"The day has been quiet until recently, with no clear trend seen. Many are thinking that the current levels are toppish and the rating news is already priced in," Sberbank dealer Pavel Sool said.

But dealers said trading livened up after U.S. payroll data were announced. They added MinFin bonds followed the rise of the Vnesh debt, which was boosted by a sharp rise in U.S. Treasuries and other markets following the payrolls news.
U.S. September payrolls fell 40,000 versus forecasts for 166,000 gain, U.S. Labor Department said on Friday.

"Prices are rising now but slower than they have been since Tuesday (on rating expectations)... Present prices are very high already but they might firm further when U.S. operators step in," one dealer said.
